seoTitle: Free Redirect Rules Converter: nginx, Apache, Netlify
metaDescription: Turn simple "from to status" lines into nginx, Apache, Caddy, Netlify _redirects or Vercel JSON redirects. Free and runs entirely in your browser.
intro: Write your redirects once as plain lines of from, to and an optional status code, then output them for nginx, Apache, Caddy, Netlify or Vercel.
why:
Redirect lists tend to live in a spreadsheet during a site migration, and then someone has to retype every row into whatever the new host expects. The syntax differs enough to cause mistakes: nginx wants a location block, Apache a Redirect directive, Netlify a bare _redirects line and Vercel a JSON array.

This tool takes one line per rule and writes the matching format, validating that each source starts with a slash and that the status is a real redirect code. It is a good fit for exact-path redirects after a URL change. Pattern rules and regular expressions still need hand-written config.
howTo: Enter one rule per line as from, to and an optional status code, such as /old /new 301.
Choose the output format: nginx, Apache, Caddy, Netlify _redirects or Vercel JSON.
Copy the result into your server config or redirects file.

faq.a: 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308. If you leave the code out it defaults to 301. Any other value stops with an error so you do not ship an invalid redirect.

faq.q: Can I use wildcards or regular expressions?
faq.a: No. Each line becomes an exact-path rule, such as location = /old in nginx. For pattern redirects, write those by hand or start from the generated block and extend it.

faq.q: Where do I paste the nginx output?
faq.a: Inside the relevant server block of your nginx config, then reload nginx. The location blocks use an exact match, so they should not clash with your catch-all location.

faq.q: Can the target be a full URL?
faq.a: Yes. The destination can be a path or an absolute URL such as https://example.com/new. The source must be a path starting with a slash.
